name: Liu Fang-p’ing
bio: Liu Fang-p’ing is dated by Giles to the 8th or 9th century AD. His poem here is a lonely woman’s spring.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: The Spinster
poems.author: Liu Fang-p’ing

poems.title: A Moonlight Night
poems.author: Liu Fang-p’ing
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
When the moon has coloured half the house,
With the North Star at its height and the South Star setting,
I can feel the first motions of the warm air of spring
In the singing of an insect at my green-silk window.

poems.title: Spring Heart-break
poems.author: Liu Fang-p’ing
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
With twilight passing her silken window,
She weeps alone in her chamber of gold;
For spring is departing from a desolate garden,
And a drift of pear-petals is closing a door.
